messages.subject: sem: mediation with binary outcome
parts:
Hello,

I am doing a simple mediation in lavaan: three latent IVs, one latent mediator (both measures continuous), and one binary outcome.

I encountered different ways how to estimate the model and I am wondering which one I should use.

1) fit_donation <- sem(donation, data = mydata, ordered = "Donated").

2) fit_donation_2 = sem(donation, data = mydata, estimator='dwls', ordered= "Donated")

3) fit_donation_3 = sem(donation, data = mydata, estimator='WLSM', ordered="Donated")

The obtained output differs with these three estimations.

With the first estimation, I get two columns, standard and robust (I guess robust should be used?). While RMSEA is pretty much the same in both columns (.05/0.7), CFI decreased from .96 to .82 in the latter column.

With the second estimation, I obtain only one column and it has good model fit indices.

With the third estimation, I get again two columns but in this case in both columns CFI is above .90 and RMSEA difference between two columns a bit more than in the case of the first estimation (.05/.09).

What is the reason for the difference in results, and how to decide on which estimation to use?

Thanks!

Best,

Aneta

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: sem: mediation with binary outcome
parts: What is the reason for the difference in results, and how to decide on which estimation to use?

Find the description of the estimator= argument on the ?lavOptions help page to see that the default in your first call will be estimator="WLSMV", which is "DWLS" with robust settings for the se= and test= arguments.  You should always pay attention to robust stats when they are available, and they are necessary for valid inference with DWLS.
